bounded_predicate: Opt-in style convention: inspect direct catch clauses, map a catch whose first body child is a throw with thrown-expression text exactly equal to the catch parameter name, then report only the trailing contiguous nonnull suffix via takeLastWhile. The finding entity is the whole throw expression. No rule-specific options.

positive.intent: A valid callback boundary catches IOException only to rethrow the same instance. This is redundant scaffolding under the explicitly selected style convention, not swallowed-exception or cancellation detection.

negative.intent: The catch performs a caller-controlled recording action before rethrowing the same instance. The selected rule remains active and does not match a first-child rethrow; no assurance about the callback or exception-flow safety is implied.

suppression.intent: Genuine file-scoped upstream suppression only on the package-isolated copy. Preserve every positive range from the byte-identical unsuppressed neighbor. No host finding filter or ktChecker-ID suppression alias.

controls.intent: Parentheses do not change the rethrown instance, but thrown-expression text is (failure), not failure. Retain the anticipated syntactic false negative instead of normalizing the source or claiming propagation proof.

The later disjoint IllegalStateException catch performs recovery. takeLastWhile stops on that worked catch, so the earlier redundant IOException rethrow is exempt. This exercises the actual ordered-suffix predicate, not a body-effect or reachability analysis.

The same disjoint recovery catch now precedes the IOException rethrow. The trailing rethrow still reports despite the earlier work. Preserve this opt-in policy limit and the source/documentation ordering discrepancy; do not describe all worked multi-catch blocks as exempt.

limitations: This is an explicit opt-in info/style/intent-dependent rule, not a mandatory correctness rewrite. Intentional propagation boundaries can be legitimate.
Only the first catch-body child and exact thrown-expression text are inspected. Parenthesized spelling is an anticipated miss; an earlier body statement prevents the match.

The actual implementation reports a trailing contiguous suffix of violating catches. The documentation saying any worked catch exempts the block is broader than the actual ordered predicate; both orderings are independently retained.
No type resolution, cancellation detection, swallowing analysis, cleanup effect, reachability, ownership, resource lifetime or coroutine graph proof is delivered.
No rule-specific options exist. The standard disabled lifecycle control is not a fabricated genuine-option demonstration.

six_case_plan.positive: Run the exact owner-selected syntax route on these immutable source bytes. Expected ranges are authored from the pinned predicate, never observed output.
six_case_plan.negative: Run the independent valid alternative with this SAME rule active and require an enabled upstream descriptor even with no finding.
six_case_plan.configuration: Replay original positive bytes with the selected rule explicitly disabled. This is a separately counted configuration control, never a scope/default-activation reduction.
six_case_plan.version: Replay positive bytes under the pinned CLI; require a fresh per-cohort version probe and two per-rule Common/Native abstentions. Modeled baseline 2.4.21 versus parser 2.4.10 remains unqualified.
six_case_plan.suppression: Use genuine upstream file annotation only on an additional package-isolated copy; the unsuppressed original neighbor must keep every expected range.
six_case_plan.regression: Seal the negative correction as the child of suppression, delete the obsolete suppressed copy, and verify both registered parent and child unchanged.

qualification_note: Authored ranges/intents are not observed diagnostics. Retain unexpected/false-positive outputs and all misses; never rewrite expectations to force a pass. All three rules require explicit owner opt-in and retain info/intent-dependent classification. Real isolated runner, active descriptor, source snapshots and fresh source-bound evidence require separate root admission.
